messages:
Amy: Quick follow-up from the policy DSL RFC — we need to lock down the admission/eval contract. Do we keep policy as a synchronous per-request call (simple but adds p95) or a fast cached decision + async authoritative check (complex but better p95)?
Ben: I lean sync for the first pass. Easier to reason about and rollback.
Carla: Sync will blow our latency if evals get heavier (more matchers, geo checks). We should at least have a fast-path cache in front.
Ed: Two-level sounds pragmatic: cheap sidecar scoring for hot path, authoritative policy service for accounting/consistency. Sidecar returns immediate decision + provenance.
Frank: If we do sidecars, cache invalidation across regions is hairy. Need TTL, versioned keys, and an invalidate message bus.
Gina: Example DSL sketch to discuss scoring shape (pseudo):
```policy
route_rule "cost_latency_mix" {
  match { tenant.tier in ["free","standard"] }
  score = cost * 1.25 + latency_ms * 0.75
  prefer region = local if score_delta < 5
}
```
Gina: The key is deterministic scores and a bounded numeric space so runtime can compare/aggregate.
policy-bot: NOTE: new policy API must include policy_version and reason for explainability. Canary header = X-Policy-Version.
Amy: Questions we should resolve this week: 1) wire contract for sidecar <-> control plane, 2) cache key semantics & TTL, 3) version compatibility story for runtimes, 4) rollout plan (canary + automatic rollback).
Ben: I'll prototype a minimal POST /policy/eval shape:
```
POST /policy/eval
{ tenant_id, model, input_signature, region_hints }
--> { decision: "accept"|"fallback"|"queue", score: 12.3, policy_version: "v2026-03-12", reason: "cost<=threshold" }
```
Carla: Add explainability limit: reason string <= 256 chars, and structured tags list for downstream analytics. Keep payload tiny.
Ed: Also include a stable request fingerprint/hash in the request so caches are stable across retries. e.g., request_hash = sha256(tenant|model|sig).
Frank: Compatibility: runtime binary should advertise supported policy_version ranges. If control plane serves an unsupported policy, runtime falls back to a safe heuristic and emits a telemetry event.
Gina: Testing: add a sim job that runs 10k synthetic requests with region churn / model hot spikes. Validate p50/p95 and correctness versus authoritative decisions.
Amy: Operational notes: control plane will expose /policy/versions and a deprecation window of 2 weeks for breaking changes. Canary rollout uses tenant opt-in header + rollout fraction.
Ben: Implementation owners: Ben+Frank = sidecar lib + cache; Carla+Ed = policy service wire contract + authoritative eval; Gina = proxy canary header + sim harness; Amy = RFC addendum + rollout checklist.
Carla: One more: fallback semantics need to be explicit. If sidecar says fallback->model_variant_B but authoritative later disagrees, we should surface both decisions in logs and allow automatic reconciliation, not silent override.
Ed: Agree. Reconciliation rules: sidecar decision is immediate; authoritative decision can tag the request result with final_decision and trigger compensating metrics. No retroactive cancellation of already-sent responses.
Frank: Security: policy evals may include tenant signals; ensure sidecar doesn't leak cross-tenant state and encrypt policy_version in transit.
Gina: I'll add a checklist item for end-to-end perf profiling before canary.
Amy: Good. I'll draft the follow-up RFC addendum today and tag owners. Meeting to sync on implementation scope Friday 10:00am.
Ben: :thumbsup:
Carla: ack
Ed: ack
Frank: ack
Gina: ack
